title: DR1's declaration has the user confirm they are complying with Regulation (EU) 2017/625 including on animal health and welfare; the frontend's declaration never says it.

controls.text: I am the contact for the authorities and located in the UK.

finding.frontend: The declaration's first clause is a heading standing alone — "I am the contact for the authorities and located in the UK." — with nothing under it (`src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/declaration/template.njk:10`). The user ticks one box at the foot of the page to confirm the whole declaration, so they confirm this clause as a statement about where they are and nothing more.
finding.prototype: DR1 gives the same clause a sentence of its own underneath: "I am complying with the requirements of Regulation (EU) 2017/625 including on animal health and welfare." (`app/views/declaration.html:41-42`). It is what turns the clause from a statement of location into a statement of legal compliance, and it is the only place in either service's declaration where the governing regulation is named.
finding.difference: Add the sentence under the first declaration clause, as a paragraph below the heading. One new key in the declaration copy and one line in the template. This is legal text on a page whose only purpose is a legal confirmation, so take DR1's wording unchanged rather than paraphrasing it, and add the Welsh string alongside.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding any mention of Regulation (EU) 2017/625 on the frontend's declaration page or in its copy file.

relatedTo.why: Both are clauses of the same declaration and both need the same legal sign-off before the copy changes.
